chunks: The followers of two different religions do not inherit from one another. A Muslim inherits from a disbeliever, but a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim.
That is because the foundational ruling regarding the wealth of the polytheists is that it is fay' for the Muslims, and the Muslims have more right to it than the polytheists.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only forbade inheritance to the disbelievers as a punishment for their disbelief, just as He forbade it to the killer as a punishment for his killing.
As for the Muslim, then for what crime and punishment should he be deprived of inheritance? And how could Islam make his condition worse, along with the saying of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?

key_terms.أَهْلُ مِلَّتَيْنِ: followers of two different religions or confessional communities
key_terms.الْقَاتِلِ: the killer, cited as an analogy for being barred from inheritance
key_terms.الْكَافِرُ: the disbeliever; here, the non-Muslim excluded from inheriting from a Muslim
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثَ: inheritance or estate transfer after death
key_terms.عُقُوبَةً: a punitive consequence or legal deprivation
key_terms.فَيْءٌ: property classified as fay'; wealth reverting to the Muslim community without ordinary inheritance entitlement

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim inherit from a non-Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that inheritance does not pass mutually between followers of two different religions, while affirming that a Muslim may inherit from a disbeliever but not the reverse. It frames this rule within a broader juridical principle about the property of polytheists and presents the disbeliever’s exclusion from inheritance as a punitive consequence of kufr, not something that should disadvantage the Muslim through Islam.
